items.title: How much does bundling steps together actually cost?
items.description: Models the safe-refactor loop's core trade-off: if each individual structural step carries some small, independent chance of quietly changing behavior in a way a shared end-of-batch test run won't obviously catch (a canceled-out effect, a case the tests don't cover), bundling more steps into one commit before running tests compounds that risk instead of adding it. At the discipline's default — one step, then test, then commit (n=1) — the risk is just that one step's own error rate. Drag the batch size up to 6 to reproduce Boxtree's own worked example: bundling all six of its refactoring steps into a single commit instead of six separate ones roughly quintuples the chance something slipped through undetected, from 5% to over 26%.

params.name: perStepErrorRate
params.label: Chance a single step quietly changes behavior

items.compute: const n = params.stepsPerCommit; const p = params.perStepErrorRate / 100; const risk = 1 - Math.pow(1 - p, n); return { riskOfUndetectedChange: risk * 100 };

outputs.label: Risk at least one step's behavior slip goes undetected
